# Managed recognition with held Live finalization

5 October 2026: two unchanged-release application processes independently exercise managed CPU Qwen recognition followed by a held Codex Live final rewrite. A native comparison matches all eleven observed states, three complete stable-window RGB observations, full History/rewrite rows, retained PCM, public review/recording feedback and authenticated speech requests. The existing bootstrap process owner extends to these cases; the assembled [Live editor owner](live-editor-evidence.md) retains its separate longer-document geometry and I/O-failure contracts.

| Actual application action | Independently observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Record eight seconds, then Stop | Two provisional rewrite turns; complete final speech enters History and the final rewrite waits. Copy is refused without changing the clipboard. |
| Edit the public Live text box while final rewrite waits | The old result is discarded after release. A fourth turn receives the edited draft, saves the reconciled final text with that edit, and copies it. Review Copy becomes available afterward. |
| Cancel the held final rewrite | The original dictation remains, no rewrite row is saved, clipboard stays untouched and the rewrite process/workspace are gone before the release gate is opened. |

[The frozen fixture](released-bootstrap-managed-live.json), SHA-256 `224f46bed6231de3d43a71d8115906978c072b8d241e711aae4672192a19142a`, contains only independently collected release results. It shares the earlier [managed-capture fixture](released-bootstrap-managed-capture.json)'s configuration and fixed public input through explicit overrides; earlier oracles are unchanged. Original source/native observations are `tmp/qwen-joined-live-clipboard/session.hYzsaG/qwen-joined-live/results.json`, SHA-256 `f344518e8c42fab8680221d46d2c8bc97be00ea6fbe616d418e45871dfd2857a`. All 91 packaged source modules/resources match immutable commit `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f` before launch. No application handler or callback is patched, directly invoked by the observer or substituted.

Both variants receive 256,000 bytes of the same pinned public 16 kHz mono PCM, in real 320-byte fragments paced at 32,000 bytes/second. Controlled native Qwen/Codex endpoints and sparse readiness metadata exercise ordinary managed clients and actual authenticated HTTP/RPC; they do not run model inference. Each case makes three speech requests in one resident runtime. The edit case makes four Codex turns, the cancellation case three. Complete prompt/model/effort inputs, History columns, reply metadata, WAV format/input hashes, sampled public statuses, visible text boxes and relevant button sensitivity remain compared.

Only validated generated UUIDs, creation timestamps/retained filenames, recognition time and sampled recording elapsed/level normalize. The existing managed owner also normalizes runtime PID/key paths and health retry counts while preserving complete health-status sets and unauthenticated health checks. Stable 1100×800 RGB windows match `29c274f9980f3ae749763a88f5bb640c8a4f0ef78f9244b425c02cd832de4de3` after edited finalization/Copy and `0bd29c1b410ffd3f2d47bba069d165eb63953fceb3e7a0fff33d4b6251b69246` after Cancel. Pending frames remain in the raw observations without a transient-pixel assertion or mask.

The native check reads public GTK D-Bus actions/status, actual SQLite/WAVs, public AT-SPI text/action interfaces and whole private X11 windows from separate processes. Editing uses the observed `Live draft` text-box role; its equally named label is a different accessibility object. The actual Cancel button exposes `Cancel` in this GTK environment. Copy uses the genuine private-session `xclip`, also made available to the independently restricted application PATH. Initial observer label/PATH assumptions are preserved separately in `tmp/qwen-joined-live/independent.log` and `corrected.log`, excluded from accepted evidence.

The first maintained attempt matched all six edit states but waited for pipe EOF after acknowledged app exit: the legitimate external X11 selection owner inherited those descriptors. `tmp/qwen-joined-live/native-owner.log` and its stage records preserve that excluded harness stall. The corrected owner observes app exit and a file log without killing or shortening the clipboard owner. These are test-support changes; production behavior and installed payloads are unchanged.

The final workspace-built owner passes all eleven Live states alongside its unchanged bootstrap/managed Stop/Cancel/cold-record/startup-fault contracts in `tmp/qwen-joined-live/gated-owner-final.log`, taking 121.91 seconds. All application logs are empty and owned Qwen/Codex processes, keys and ephemeral rewrite workspaces are gone. PID cleanup requires the actual `/proc` entry to disappear, including zombies, matching the source observer. The X11 selection owner intentionally remains available until clipboard replacement/private-session teardown. Actual `make linux-test` passes 141 ordinary tests, zero failures and 71 ignored checks across 98 suites, both strict Clippy variants, formatting and generated consistency in `tmp/qwen-joined-live/full-gate-final.log`. Test support shares window placement, stores and protocol normalization with the existing managed owner; the compact fixture is 36,799 bytes, with no new ignored test or production code.

Use the prerequisites and private process-owner invocation in [managed-capture evidence](bootstrap-managed-capture-evidence.md). The same owner now includes both Live cases and requires the development `codex-fixture-peer` binary alongside the audio/Qwen/credential peers. These binaries and the temporary Python release collector are excluded from distribution; maintained checks run natively.

The [worker lifecycle record](../../../../docs/verification/rust-worker-lifecycle/README.md#joined-live-finalization-and-manual-revisions) links the final owner/gate receipts and acceptance limits. This isolated X11 check does not verify physical microphone/F9/F10, Wayland/portal delivery, all Live configurations/providers, restart recovery, transient rendering or every supported platform. It adds bounded process-level evidence without closing a complete-workflow matrix row or authorizing release/installation.
